(a) Short Title.—This title may be cited as the “Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Amendments Act”. 
    (b) References to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995.—Except as otherwise expressly provided, whenever in this title an amendment or repeal is expressed in terms of an amendment to, or repeal of, a section or other provision, the reference shall be considered to be made to a section or other provision of the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995 (16 U.S.C. 5601 et seq.).

fable.w: This section only provides a short title and a rule of construction for references to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995. The tempting reading is that a fisheries convention implies commissions or stakeholder consultation, but nothing in this text sets up any process involving a party outside the federal government in a federal decision. The mere appearance of a proper noun is not participation.
fable.s: This title may be cited as the “Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Amendments Act”.

qwen_block.w: This section contains only boilerplate provisions regarding the short title of the act and how to interpret references to existing statutes. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory committees, or coordination with outside parties. Therefore, it does not involve participation.
qwen_block.s: (a) Short Title.—This title may be cited as the “Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Amendments Act”. (b) References to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995.—Except as otherwise expressly provided, whenever in this title an amendment or repeal is expressed in terms of an amendment to, or repeal of, a section or other provision, the reference shall be considered to be made to a section or other provision of the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995 (16 U.S.C. 5601 et seq.).

opus.w: This section only gives the short title and a rule for reading references to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995. It sets up no process for anyone outside the federal government to take part in a federal decision. The word "Convention" may suggest international or outside parties, but here it is just part of a proper noun.
opus.s: This title may be cited as the “Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Amendments Act”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is purely procedural, establishing the short title of the act and providing instructions on how to interpret references to the Northwest Atlantic Fisheries Convention Act of 1995. It does not contain any language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. There are no mentions of public hearings, advisory committees, state/tribal consultation, or public comment periods.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this is an amendment to a convention act, it implies international cooperation or consultation. However, the text itself is purely procedural, defining the short title and how to interpret references to the existing statute. It contains no language requiring consultation, public comment, hearings, or interaction with outside parties.
